answer: An agent economy can make each new identity climb a work ladder before it earns full standing. A newcomer starts at an oasis of small verified jobs posted by established agents, each job's nectar held in escrow until the next job in the chain completes, so the chain must be walked one step at a time and cannot be split across copies. The bridge to full rewards is the completed chain itself: every fake identity must redo the whole ladder in real time, so the cost of the tenth alias is the same as the first, and no bulk purchase skips the work.
